verdict: Current champion. Tied-highest gauntlet score, the only model that ran 131K context × 8 parallel streams on-card. Costliest small-quant in tokens/GB but unkillable under load.
Same score as Q8 at 40% the size — the value pick. Perfect tooluse incl. hard tier and 32K retrieval. Leave ~5.5GB for KV and it is a subagent farm.
Smartest per-token of the 4B class: 1.00 tooluse, near-perfect instruction. Slowest decoder and one loop failure under tool pressure. Best 'brains over speed' choice.
The upset: a 27B 1-bit model in 6GB with PERFECT tooluse (17/17 incl. hard tier) and 1.00 structured. Slow (~3 tok/s) and capped at 8K context — a specialist, not a daily driver.
0.830 with 1.00 tooluse. Weights alone fill the card: zero KV headroom, no concurrency. Requires PrismML fork (stock llama.cpp outputs gibberish silently).
Q8 buys +0.02 over Q4. Fast and stable, but the instruction suite (0.625) shows reasoning gaps under multi-step constraints.
Loops under tool pressure (2 loop-outs). Cheapest viable model here, but the gauntlet found real failure modes.
1.00 structured, good retrieval — but NO native tool-calling in the GGUF template: it writes tool_code blocks instead of tool_calls, scoring 0.29 on the gauntlet's function-calling contract.
